sections.title: Responses: What They Answer, and Whether They Were Consumed
What a turn asks of the owner
AI ↔ AI Multi-Agent with Chain Depth
SIP Call → Unified process_inbound with Protocol Traces

links.scope: Closed-room inbound, direct record, direct send and response refusals; a hook closing its current pass; archived-room inbound refusal.
missing: Streaming, externally changed status, regeneration and replacement records are supplied by the complementary lifecycle link. Optional voice entry paths need their own capability evidence.

links.scope: Response and injected passes, deleted rooms, bound replacement records, streaming boundaries, member records and regeneration while the room closes.
missing: Optional voice/conference entry paths require capability-specific evidence. Internal read-count optimizations are permitted, not required, by §5.1.

links.scope: Five public transitions from all four room statuses, no-op/refusal state and notice stability, and organization checks before overdue timers.
missing: The public read matrix and retained-channel gates are supplied by the complementary lifecycle links. Optional voice paths need their own capability evidence.
Snapshot equality alone cannot prove absence of identical writes on every persistent backend; specialized effect tests retain that responsibility.

links.scope: Public history, bindings and member reads at all four room statuses, organization isolation, missing resources and timeline cursors.
missing: This read link does not by itself prove every retained-channel write gate; those are covered by the complementary refusal links. Optional voice session teardown is outside the Level 0 scope.

links.scope: Named timer-check scope, overdue timers before public transitions, explicit/message resumption, timer-setting activity preservation, and timer closure before inbound.
missing: The complementary timer link supplies direct gates, sweeps, cancellation and concurrent-write source evidence. Atomic persistent-store transactions and paused sender/group routing retain their separate store/routing evidence.

links.scope: Due timers at direct mutations and response passes; activity exclusions; inert checks; all-page scoped sweeps; cancellation and concurrent commits before and after the status write.
missing: The shared runner cannot force a store-write interleaving or caller cancellation; the specialized source tests and corresponding Rust runtime tests are required alongside these receipts. Atomic persistent-store commits and paused automatic routing are covered in the store/routing areas rather than certified by this timer link.

links.scope: Caller outcomes retain successful and refused provider receipts; clean sets store none, partial failures keep all target outcomes, excluding the source.
missing: Real provider adapters and cancellation exception forms are specialized tests. A scripted output is not a proof that a vendor accepted or rejected a send. Generic transport-provider parity is outside this bounded lot.

links.scope: Local tool-call composition: cumulative character counts, slot identity and order, size coalescing, terminal frames, retry/fallback isolation, visibility and absence of partial call persistence.
missing: Provider wire parsing, distributed executors and publication failures are not established by these scenarios.
Wall-clock coalescing is not covered here; forced consumer abandonment and cross-family order have separate native source evidence.
The rest of this broad clause, including all stored tool outcome combinations, remains outside this link.

links.scope: Public realtime observations when a composing turn is cancelled, exceeds its loop budget or its caller is abandoned.
missing: Does not establish every provider or distributed executor lifecycle, nor wall-clock coalescing.

links.scope: Chat Completions tool-call composition, through the actual provider decoder and public room bus on simulated HTTP responses.
missing: Does not establish every provider protocol, remote service behavior, distributed executor or publication failure.
Wall-clock coalescing and all other outcomes of this broad clause remain outside this source link.

links.scope: A deferred turn's long answered input stays whole through one or two context overflows; later rounds build on the compacted request, keep call/result pairs and store the first long result while retaining recent results.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: A generation hook reconstructs a deferred turn's unchanged input. Emergency compaction keeps that entire input and later messages, and subsequent memory compactions and requests retain the same boundary.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: A real Discussion delays a turn while later messages arrive. Between tool rounds, compact receives only the history before the answered input; a returned summary preserves that input, the later messages, runtime notes and tool pairs, even after an emergency or initial-memory summary.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: A generation hook reconstructs a deferred turn's unchanged input, at the same position (identical questions included) or at a unique moved position. Between tool rounds the memory receives exactly the history before that input and the generation usage; its summary keeps the input, later messages, runtime notes and tool pairs whole.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: Full-value association of deferred inputs after generation hooks; exact protected context and empty memory history when ambiguous, explicit overflow failure without replay, subsequent tool results shortened only when eligible, and unchanged ordinary-turn behavior.
missing: Multipart input matching and deferred-tool reopening combined with ambiguous inputs are outside these shared scenarios.

links.scope: In-place mutation, replacement, mutation followed by copying and input removal preserve historical tool results and memory additions while shortening only earlier new results, in both generation modes.
missing: Other input transformations and emergency overflow are covered by separate shared scenarios.

links.scope: All four access values, crossed with mute, for inbound and directly injected source events and for transport/intelligence targets.
missing: Buffered and streamed response permissions, regenerated answers and permission changes during an in-flight turn are not exhaustively mapped by this link.

links.scope: A statically muted readable transport or intelligence binding still receives the event and contributes tasks and observations.
missing: Streaming mute transitions, unread stream closure, output_muted and mute/unmute lifecycle semantics remain outside this link.

links.scope: Public visibility inputs, committed text events and per-agent model context on the in-memory backend.
missing: Framework-created internal records and all non-public event producers are not covered by this public-door matrix.

All six public doors plus hook restoration, channel response visibility and depth-limit records; framework internal-record protection is specialized source evidence.
missing: Framework-created record paths across voice/media and outside-pipeline commits are not exhaustively linked; warning logs are checked only by specialized Python tests.

links.scope: Public visibility inputs, committed text events and per-agent model context on the in-memory backend.
missing: EDIT/DELETE target visibility narrowing, non-text content and every refusal/reentry path remain outside this mapping.
Streaming permission changes and all memory summarizer inputs need separate proofs.

links.scope: Rules 1-3 and 5 for static bindings: source refusal, readable targets, retained target effects and self-skip. Visibility is all throughout these matrices.
missing: Rules 4 and 6-8 (visibility, derived bindings, revocation and reconstructed context) require separate mappings.
Rule 2 response paths, hooks changing permissions, streaming transitions and unbound sources are outside the matrices.
Rule 3 hook-returned effects on refused messages are outside this link.

links.scope: Rule 2 read-only/mute stream precedence and rule 8 refused/deleted reader history, live edits and unfiltered host histories.
missing: This does not cover every permission rule, live permission transitions during a stream, arbitrary memory providers or distributed stores. Hook contexts and pure structural views use specialized tests, not shared scenario observations.

links.scope: Empty-room indexes, consecutive per-room commits and counters, concurrent writers, hard-deletion gaps, and every major pipeline commit path.
missing: A persistent-store uniqueness constraint and atomic allocation across independent connection owners require specialized store tests, beyond the shared runner. The model compatibility check is specialized too; a scenario receipt does not execute it.

links.scope: Twelve sends with one key under one locked hook return the original id and content without consuming its ten-pass budget; a following fresh send still commits.
missing: Other budget entry points, off-lock adoption, task lifetimes and concurrent deadlines retain their own specialized tests and existing scenarios.

links.scope: Forty-five buffered answers and forty-five hook notices fit separate budgets of fifty. Exact turn counts and transport deliveries reject prematurely capped work.
missing: Streaming segments and notices above the hook cap are separate Python variants, not proven by this buffered case. Optional voice and orchestration paths and mutation-hook recursion remain outside this link.

links.scope: Response visibility intersections, propagation through a two-agent cascade, buffered real-model streams, hook narrowing and depth-limit records.
missing: Transport-produced answers, instruction and delegation cascade boundaries, concurrent binding changes and every streamed tool-row path remain outside this link.

links.scope: Named executor hooks: refusal of invalid names/modes and collisions, stable equal-priority activation order and per-trigger replacement.
missing: This link does not establish every trigger, filter, off-lock ordering rule or distributed registration path of the broad clause.

links.scope: Timer hooks receive one final stored context, including activity committed after the status write.
missing: Other lifecycle triggers retain their separate evidence; this link covers timer contexts only. The concurrent interleaving is proven by specialized source/runtime tests, not by a shared scenario receipt.

links.scope: BEFORE_BROADCAST through process_inbound, including fail-open/fail-closed behavior where configured.
missing: Other SYNC triggers and wrong payload types; exception-specific logging is not exhaustively asserted.

links.scope: BEFORE_BROADCAST through process_inbound, including fail-open/fail-closed behavior where configured.
missing: Other SYNC chain triggers and wrong payload types.

links.scope: BEFORE_BROADCAST through process_inbound, including fail-open/fail-closed behavior where configured.
missing: Falsy modifications and their propagation on string/dict payloads; wrong types.

links.scope: BEFORE_BROADCAST through process_inbound, including fail-open/fail-closed behavior where configured.
missing: Other invalid-result forms and triggers; sixth-level composite exception.

links.scope: AI text-channel human input: notification-independent answers, timeout precedence and refusal versus failure.
missing: Voice and conference doors; handler-native retention and lifecycle proofs are outside these shared assertions.

links.scope: BEFORE_BROADCAST cannot widen or clear an answer scope, write internal visibility or widen a framework internal record.
missing: Replacement identity, authority fields, instruction marks and every hook trigger remain outside this scope. Framework voice record creation is Level 3; its visibility protection is specialized source evidence.

links.scope: Injection pass ordering, off-lock collection, refusal before storage, authority and mutation recipients, next-turn history, plus specialized cancellation, late-failure and Python model-transport evidence.
missing: Rust realtime/model-transport ingestion is not implemented or exercised by this core lot. Python silent-ingestion source evidence is linked, but does not certify Rust voice conformance (RMK-333).
Gate refusal is sampled at duplicate detection and room closure, with timeout after collection; this does not exhaust every pre-storage gate or every mutation revalidation race.

links.scope: An INSTRUCTION returned by BEFORE_BROADCAST is dropped before its own pass; ordinary injections, tasks and observations remain.
All fourteen Python SYNC trigger names in the generic engine, BEFORE_DELIVER and ON_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED end-to-end, and identity challenge exceptions. Rust implements ten of these trigger names.
missing: End-to-end warning assertions for each typed turn and voice caller remain outside this mapping. Rust has no BEFORE_BRIDGE_AUDIO, BEFORE_BRIDGE_VIDEO, ON_SPEAK_DECISION or ON_VISION_RESULT; the Python engine tests do not certify those Rust features.

links.scope: Step 2 only: explicit/custom routing, room creation, scoped refusal, auto-attach defaults, correspondent record before hooks and re-routing.
missing: The rest of the inbound pipeline has separate links and is not completed here. Ordering at parse/identity/commit boundaries, lifecycle completion, locks and cancellation retain specialized tests and previous lots. No complete credit is claimed for this composite unit.

links.scope: Named calls draw their room work budget before the inbound rate bucket and address callbacks. A cap refusal consumes no rate token; an already empty bucket does not mask the cap; a rate refusal still consumes one work unit.
missing: The rest of the inbound pipeline and its failure paths are outside this preflight slice.
Native tests are source references here; their executions and Rust local gates are retained separately, not treated as scenario execution receipts.

links.scope: Running and queued cascades are isolated, including a second room on the same channel; cancellation preserves transport delivery, the first reason and completed outcomes.
missing: Caller-task cancellation, Python async finalizer ordering, cancellation suppression, setup failure, handed-over turns and close deadlines require specialized proofs. Shared background waits guarantee final outcomes, not that every waiter was polled before cancellation. Distributed backends are not certified.

links.scope: A greeting and a streamed segment do not advance the delivered cursor while their transport waits; a later public send follows the held greeting.
missing: The source Python test also injects an internal lane plan directly. Multi-worker persistence and lock deadlines require the separate distributed suites; no performance bound is inferred.

links.scope: The transport direction gate: both directions execute on_event, only an outbound-capable transport is delivered to.
missing: Other broadcast steps, capabilities, retries, rates, concurrent delivery and intelligence execution are covered separately or remain unmapped.

links.scope: Recipient contracts, access, mute, visibility, side effects, target delivery, transcoding and retained outcomes at the broadcast boundary.
missing: Provider-specific normalization remains specialized, with RMK-1392 retaining its existing corners. Broadcast concurrency is checked for twelve targets, not a throughput claim. Rate limiting, breaker state transitions and all retry policies retain specialized suites.

links.scope: The delivered event follows the recent-event window supplied to the target.
missing: No certification of every intelligence memory backend or provider history rendering.

links.scope: Deleted text and edited text are withheld from later model calls; specialized tests retain event identity and remove raw payloads and media edit content while hooks keep audit content.
missing: All native provider references and channel_data, every parse/delivery history boundary, arbitrary media content, window eviction and distributed stores are not exhaustively covered by these assertions.

links.scope: Explicit and custom room ids; scoped identity and metadata; null answers and anonymous senders; organization refusal before attachment and commit.
missing: Custom-router authentication depends on integrator policy and needs operational review. Identity lookup counts and stale reads require specialized tests. Provider normalization corners remain on RMK-1392; callback binding replacement ordering remains on RMK-1422.

links.scope: Newest binding then participant selection, creation-time ties, paused conversations and organization/channel scoping.
missing: Shared cases do not cover every participant status and connected_via variant. Specialized source and Rust store tests retain those assertions. Stored-recipient normalization differences remain on RMK-1374.

links.scope: Single-conversation admission, correspondent retention and anonymous/group behavior; rechecks under the room lock and during room creation.
missing: Paging, real lock deadlines, exact default-router and identity-store call counts, creation conflicts, and attach-then-wait ordering require specialized tests. The unreadable-recipient scenario covers a boolean; the specialized Python matrix covers objects, lists and floats, both routing strategies and log privacy. RMK-1422 retains the callback ordering edge.

links.scope: Recipient statuses select the newest ACTIVE or PAUSED room; explicit statuses preserve payload across lifecycle states and do not change activity, counters or updated_at. Async observers ignore event filters and do not hold the caller.
missing: Webhook parsing remains provider-specific. This link does not certify every tenant/custom-address implementation or hook scheduling primitive.

links.scope: A binding speaks only for its channel; another correspondent receives neither stored history nor deliveries from the selected conversation.
missing: Cross-number store queries and some identity connected_via variants are specialized evidence, not per-scenario executions. Provider-specific forms retain their separate contract tests.

links.scope: An ambiguous channel returns null directly and creates a separate room end to end, leaving old timelines, bindings and deliveries unchanged.
missing: The operational obligation for integrators to authenticate a custom strategy or supply a trusted explicit room needs review outside the library.

links.scope: Repeated default queries at unchanged state, explicit creation timestamps with reverse insertion, and custom strategy inputs.
missing: Specialized backend query tests remain necessary; shared in-memory and SQLite executions are not a proof for every backend. Custom strategy determinism itself is the integrator responsibility.

links.scope: A missing named hook refuses placement before handover and preserves the previous successful turn.
missing: Channel calls, post-handover failures, process restarts and other per-room state transitions are not established by this test.

links.scope: Channel-call to turn continuity, post-handover cancellation, bounded local state and retry of failed or interrupted stale-state cleanup.
missing: Remote placement, process restart and every cache owned by a concrete channel remain outside this local contract.
The Rust JSON value boundary cannot construct arbitrary unserializable Python objects; the native serialization ordering is reviewed separately.

links.scope: Only changed per-room state is persisted; later calls and turns restore it, empty state is removed, detach forgets it even on callback failure or cancellation.
missing: The reserved metadata namespace write filters and restoration on a different process are not established by this link.

links.scope: Local attached-channel verbs: JSON result, null, typed errors, validation, organization scope, changed state before error, detach and closed executor/kit refusal.
missing: Distributed placement, executor factories, replacement and process transport remain deferred in Rust.
Committed-event delivery and channel release are distinct controls, not established by these scenarios.

links.scope: The kit's local executor: per-room activation, per-trigger replacement, selection captured at request time, current definitions, missing-name refusal and strategy cleanup.
missing: Remote executors, declaration-only channels and every executor placement outcome remain outside this local proof.
Planner, speaking-policy and thinker triggers remain explicit API gaps; executor-only close has its separate local lifecycle evidence link.

links.scope: A closed local executor refuses later live-channel turns while transport-only rooms remain usable.
missing: Distributed placement, declaration-only channels, committed events and public channel_call are outside this link.

links.scope: Independent executor closure ends an admitted generation or streaming tool; self-spared work survives owner cancellation but a later external close still cuts it.
missing: Other cancellation sources, arbitrary external executors and every distributed drainage condition of the broad clause are not established by this link.

links.scope: Closing the kit's local executor: admission, active work, borrowed channels, own and ancestor turns, independent deliveries, repeated closes and later owner cancellation.
missing: Remote executor construction, transport shutdown and executor-owned channel factories remain deferred in Rust and are not established by these local scenarios.
Native source references complement the scenarios; they are not additional shared-scenario execution receipts.

links.scope: A local channel call inherits the calling turn and host, so closing its executor spares that turn.
missing: Other executor closure paths have separate evidence; distributed control transport is not established here.

links.scope: Public operation admission and delivery-key cancellation during and after the kit close; an already-entered nested scope read under a locked hook keeps its parent grace.
missing: The rest of the shutdown matrix still needs assertion-by-assertion audit: retained delivery and cursor holes, stubborn cleanup, delegation and callbacks, streaming partial responses and adapter-specific resources.
Previously deferred status-bus and failed delivery-record boundaries remain deferred by their maintainer decisions; this scenario proves none of them.

links.scope: Open-store reads, late status and observer admission; native cursor placement and unfinished call results. Local core shutdown only.
missing: The shutdown annex still tracks delegation completion, response placement, commit-before-observer ordering, work added during close and hand-back composition.
Media, service-backed and remote-executor variants are not credited by local memory-store witnesses; existing maintainer deferrals remain explicit.

links.scope: Answers placed during delivery aftermath: an answer observer closes, or its sender closes while the answer is explicitly retained. Local core shutdown only.
missing: Commit-before-observer ordering, held writes, work added during close, post-cut cleanup and streamed hand-back composition remain in the shutdown annex.
Media, service-backed and remote-executor variants are not credited by local native witnesses; existing maintainer deferrals remain explicit.

links.scope: Regeneration refusal after kit close and its cut before committed selection.
missing: Shutdown of other operations, services and separate processes is outside this link.

links.scope: Event keys scoped by room and source channel, accepted and blocked replays, blank keys, store lookups, taken-key refusals, deletion and retry after a caller leaves.
missing: Task-result publication keys, proactive publication namespaces, and replay beyond the reentry budget retain their separate task/delivery/injection evidence. A store unable to resolve a held key and a caller disappearing during commit require the linked specialized tests.

links.scope: Failed lock release during discussion regeneration, after selection or queue mutation.
missing: Other operations and external lock-manager failures are not proven by this link.

links.scope: The pre-commit timeout covers handle_inbound, refuses the call and leaves no timeline event or target delivery. Specialized source tests also cover context and nested scope reads and the direct-injection lock/hook/read matrix.
missing: The shared scenario alone covers the parser. Native source proofs cover the listed additional regions, while subscription lifetime, every adoption schedule and post-commit cancellation are separate obligations.

links.scope: Timeline predicates combine before pagination; exclusive time bounds, blocked rows, source, type and correlation filters, cursor and limit behavior.
missing: get_conversation tails and visibility-argument precedence are specialized tests. The shared model does not expose every store read or count operation; no complete store-interface claim.

links.scope: Counters agree with all commit paths; a refused key changes neither target nor sequence; unstored events reserve nothing; a slow or cancelled caller does not contradict a committed event.
missing: The rest of the store consistency clause (other record updates, metadata merging and delivery-result ownership) keeps its own evidence. A commit failure, a slow store, and caller cancellation are specialized source/runtime tests. Shared scenarios alone cannot prove transaction isolation for every backend.

links.scope: Only record_delivery_results replaces a committed row’s results; stale event/target writes preserve them. PersistencePolicy defaults, inclusion and exclusion remain covered by native and shared proofs.
missing: This composite clause also includes atomicity, idempotency, lifecycle and other records covered by previous lots. Failed-set recording reentrancy and shutdown lock timing remain explicitly deferred in RMK-1340 and RMK-1342.

links.scope: Copy-in and read ownership are checked by specialized source tests; the Rust event test mutates caller-held content and nested metadata without changing the stored row.
missing: No shared JSON scenario can observe Python object aliases. Python tests cover seven record families; the Rust native test here covers event content and metadata, while ownership of other model values follows their language contracts. Private-state copy-out retains its separate tests.

links.scope: Enabling and disabling named hooks observes the calling organization's room scope.
missing: Other room operations, identity, media admissions and distributed organization placement are outside this link.

links.scope: Text strategy tools, workers, shared transports, review limits and turns scoped to the installed room.
missing: Realtime sessions, voice strategies and active-agent session configuration remain outside these text scenarios.
Not every strategy, handoff configuration, cancellation or cross-process interleaving is exercised by these links.

links.scope: Local strategy installation, explicit override, refusal and removal; preservation of existing room contents.
missing: Full discussion replacement and lifecycle across processes, every built-in strategy configuration and voice/media execution remain outside these reviewed assertions.
Store-failure and cancellation seams need native tests; shared scenario receipts do not execute them.

links.scope: A background supervisor reads bounded worker outputs or a sanitized failure through a real model turn, and preserves its private instruction record.
missing: Other supervisor strategies, timeout and cancellation paths, and its internal release callback are outside these shared assertions.

links.scope: Local instruction admission and turn boundaries, including a first read of a stored discussion that ended (rules 7, 8, 11, 15 and 16).
missing: Other Discussion rules, queue fairness and merging, normal regeneration, transcript replay, names and dispatch require their own assertion audit.
External process failure, distributed stores and executors are not proven by these local scenarios.
Only eight methods of the 90-method candidate inventory are audited in this lot.

links.scope: Regenerated discussion turns: target selection, fallback, deduplication, queue priority, waiting/listening, depth and stored state (rule 7 and associated queue rules).
missing: Other rules in the broad Discussion clause remain outside this link.
Exact model context history, tool rounds, signed markers and cross-process failure recovery need their own evidence.

links.scope: Discussion context at turn start: answered-event order, runtime notes, own tool replay and issued-mark boundaries (rule 9).
missing: Other rules in the broad Discussion clause remain outside this link.
Memory windows and summaries, speak-policy recent history, external-agent unread history and cross-process recovery need separate evidence.

links.scope: SpeakTurn.recent includes later visible messages already in the turn context, excluding the answered event (Discussion rule 9).
missing: Rust SpeakPolicy/SpeakTurn API and its matching behavior remain unported.
Other Discussion rules and policy decisions are outside this native context assertion.

links.scope: The answered event survives built-in memory windows, budget trimming and summaries at the start of a deferred Discussion turn; visibility is applied before a summarizer reads history.
missing: Custom-memory returns of the current event are covered separately by custom-memory-current-input; these four scenarios still exercise an inner memory that omits it.
Compaction between tool rounds, emergency compaction, external-agent history and distributed recovery remain outside these retrieval scenarios.

links.scope: A custom memory may return the answered event: it reaches the model once, intact, at its place, and reducing wrappers do not count or summarize it as history.
missing: Compaction between tool rounds, emergency compaction, external-agent history and distributed recovery remain outside these retrieval scenarios.
Arbitrary synthetic messages returned by a custom memory are not matched to event IDs or rewritten by this protection.

links.scope: MemoryProvider.compact receives the model's history before the answered event and the exact generation usage after each tool round of a deferred Discussion turn.
missing: Rewritten, removed or ambiguously relocated inputs are covered separately by deferred-hook-context-protection.
Other memory providers, external agents and distributed recovery remain outside these cases.

links.scope: The initial memory read reserves the authenticated Discussion notes that the model request will contain.
missing: Other own-note producers, tool declaration and replay costs, media accounting, between-round compaction and distributed recovery are outside this assertion.

links.scope: Atomic strategy tool installation, preservation of host tools, and same-strategy reinstallation.
missing: Native Rust voice-supervisor and voice-loop reinstallation variants remain for the voice phase.
This link does not cover all host/built-in/tool-server collisions, turn-supplied tools, Tool Search filtering or discovery inventories.
Execution receipts for shared scenarios do not establish execution of the specialized reinstallation test.

links.scope: Owner-served work_in_background reads its turn snapshot for agent naming and the nested-task guard, while start_task builds the worker brief from current storage.
missing: Other context accessors, realtime calls, handler result shapes and arbitrary custom handlers are outside this mapping.

links.scope: Empty answers and message-less worker failures are handed back as failed; the child room and result retain that end after a late host cancellation.
missing: Other delegation pipeline steps, callbacks, runner refusal, telemetry and voice-session delivery are outside this shared assertion set.

links.scope: Text task hand-backs preserve the configured persona and deliver a framed result to the intended model, including the tool default recipient and a configured bound above 4000.
missing: Other delegation protocol steps, realtime session delivery, lifecycle cancellation and internal completion callbacks are outside this assertion set.

links.scope: Discussion handles in relayed task results and task_status through both owner-served and agent-owned tools; status bus identifiers remain channel ids.
missing: Other delegation-tool obligations, human input, background setup changes during a turn, and external executor/backend configurations are outside this mapping.

links.scope: Background task name and nested-task boundary through gated stored-metadata changes; empty start_task hand_back falls back to default or configured mode, explicit relay overrides post, and invalid non-empty values or an empty setup mode are refused.
missing: Other delegation tools, cancellation, concurrent setup replacement and external executor configurations are outside this mapping.

links.scope: Each of two distinct failed background tasks emits its own ON_TASK_COMPLETED hook.
missing: Task creation hooks, completed and cancelled task variants are outside this mapping.
